newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close lower amid violence fears.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close lower amid violence fears.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed down on Friday with buyers expecting prices to fall further on fears of violence fears ahead of local government polls, brokers said.
The all share index closed 1.54 points down at 617.53. Price declines led gains by 24 to 12. Tea Smallholder fell 50 cents to 22.75 rupees, Royal Ceramics fell 50 cents to 28.
"If buyers do not go up on prices and volumes, the index will stagnate for a long time, because there are no panic sellers," said Thikshan Arulampalam a trader at Lanka Securities.
Turnover was 7.2 million rupees on 310,984 shares, led by local activity. Foreign buying amounted to 12,950 rupees, and selling was 948,310.
Some brokers say buyers will not improve on prices until they are sure that the index has bottomed out after Tuesday's killing of a ruling People's Alliance lawmaker.
"Buyers just expect to buy at lower prices if there is more violence closer to the (March 21) election," said a broker at John Keells.
